extra.message: UrlUtil.validateUrl(targetUrl, request) (line 80) validates the OUTER saved-request URL (e.g. '/admin/somePage?successUrl=http://evil.com'), which passes because it is same-host/relative. Immediately after, lines 93-101 extract the embedded 'successUrl=' query value and REPLACE targetUrl with that raw, unvalidated string, then pass it straight to getRedirectStrategy().sendRedirect(request, response, targetUrl) at line 108 with no re-validation. Because this is invoked after a successful login (not on the original GET), request.getParameter("successUrl") on the current POST will typically not equal this extracted value, so LocalRedirectStrategy's own equality-based validation gate is also bypassed, and response.sendRedirect() is called with a fully attacker-controlled absolute URL. An attacker can craft a link like '/admin/login?successUrl=http://evil.com' (or any protected admin deep link with that query string) so that once an admin authenticates, they are redirected off-site — classic open redirect usable for phishing/credential harvesting.

extra.message: DocumentBuilderFactory is created and used to parse merged application-context resources (builder.parse(myStream)) without disabling DOCTYPE declarations or external entities (no setFeature("http://apache.org/xml/features/disallow-doctype-decl", true), no XMLConstants.FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING, no disabling of external-general/parameter entities). Sibling classes in the same merge subsystem — MergeManager.java (line 84) and MergeJPAPersistenceResource.java (line 117) — explicitly set disallow-doctype-decl on their DocumentBuilderFactory instances, showing this protection is the established pattern and its absence here is an XXE gap: any XML resource routed through this import-merge pipeline (including Spring 'import' processing of merged context files which can originate from module/plugin-provided resources) can define external entities to read local files or trigger SSRF/DoS during parsing.

extra.message: evaluateRule() compiles and executes arbitrary MVEL expression strings (admin-authored product/offer/customer rule text, ultimately persisted and re-evaluated against live request/customer data) via MVEL.compileExpression/executeExpression using a ParserContext that only registers helper imports (MVEL, MvelHelper, CollectionUtils) and applies no method/class whitelist, SandboxedParserConfiguration, or ClassFilter restricting reflective/Java method invocation. MVEL expressions can invoke arbitrary static/instance Java methods reachable from the classpath (e.g. via chained reflection or java.lang.Runtime/ProcessBuilder access), so any actor able to supply or influence a rule string that reaches this method (e.g. a lower-privileged 'rule builder' admin role) can achieve full server-side code execution rather than the intended constrained rule-matching capability.

extra.message: shouldUseSecureCookieIfApplicable() defaults to false ('cookies.use.secure', false), and when false, setCookieValue() unconditionally forces cookie.setSecure(false) regardless of the caller-supplied isSecure flag (lines 84-89). The sole caller, SessionFixationProtectionFilter (enabled by default via filter.sessionFixationProtection.legacy.enabled:true), sets its anti-fixation cookie only on HTTPS requests and passes isSecure=true, but out-of-the-box this security-relevant cookie is still emitted without the Secure attribute unless an operator explicitly opts in via system property, allowing it to be transmitted over a later plaintext HTTP request and intercepted on mixed HTTP/HTTPS deployments.
